# Calibration for the quota boundary guard in tests/it/quota.rs.
#
# Every entry is one code shape and the verdict the guard must reach for it.
# They live OUTSIDE the .rs tree on purpose: the guard scans the crate's own
# sources, so a sample written as a Rust literal would make the guard trip over
# its own calibration.
#
#   catch <scope> <form>   the guard MUST report this shape
#   allow <scope> <form>   the guard MUST NOT report it
#
# Scope `child` is a module INSIDE the quota tree, where Rust privacy admits
# the reach and this guard is the only enforcement. Scope `outside` is every
# other module, where the compiler already refuses and the guard watches for a
# widening of that visibility. Lines after a marker are the sample.

catch child relative constructor
let p = super::Policy::new(None, Account::default());

catch child imported constructor
use super::Policy;
let p = Policy::new(None, Account::default());

catch child policy assembled
let p = super::Policy { manual_resets: None, account };

catch child reading assembled
let r = Reading { row, policy, used, observed_at };

catch child level bound by hand
let c = super::Classified { reading, level: super::QuotaLevel::Headroom };

catch child an inherent impl on the owner type
use super::Policy;
impl Policy {
    fn assemble(account: Account) -> Self {
        Self { manual_resets: None, account }
    }
}

catch child relative threshold
let level = super::classify(95.0, None);

catch child imported threshold
use super::{Account, classify, Row};

catch child threshold imported across lines
use super::{
    Account,
    classify,
    Row,
};

catch outside qualified constructor
let p = crate::quota::Policy::new(None, Account::default());

catch outside qualified level bound by hand
let c = crate::quota::Classified { reading, level };

catch outside qualified threshold
let level = crate::quota::classify(95.0, None);

allow child the test-only constructor
let p = Policy::for_tests(Some(1), account);

allow child an empty policy
let p = Policy::default();

allow child the one level producer
let c = super::Classified::first(reading);

allow child the one reading builder
let r = super::Reading::of(policy, row);

allow outside another module's own type
pub enum Policy {
    Enabled,
}

allow outside that type's own impl
impl Policy {
    fn read() {}
}

allow outside another module's own literal
sessions: vec![Classified { candidate, status }]

allow outside another module's own classifier
let verdict = classify(&frame);

allow outside a level compared
assert_eq!(held.level(), crate::quota::QuotaLevel::Critical);

allow outside the one level producer
let c = crate::quota::Classified::first(reading);

allow outside a return type in a signature
fn quota_classified(group: &crate::quota::Group) -> crate::quota::Classified {
    crate::quota::Classified::first(quota_reading(group))
}

allow child a return type in a signature
fn policy_for(scope: &Scope, account: Account) -> Policy {
    Policy::default()
}

catch child a declaration written onto a default policy
let mut p = Policy::default();
p.manual_resets = Some(3);

catch child an account written onto a default policy
let mut p = Policy::default();
p.account = account;

catch child a level written onto a classified reading
held.level = super::QuotaLevel::Headroom;

catch child a held row written onto a classified reading
held.reading = incoming;

allow child a reported account field written while parsing
account.credits = Credits::Unlimited;
account.credits_observed_at = Some(observed_at);

allow child a level compared, not written
assert_eq!(held.level(), QuotaLevel::Critical);
